content: Michael D. Langone, Ph.D., is an American counseling psychologist with a specialized focus on the study of cultic groups and psychological manipulation. He serves as the executive director of the International Cultic Studies Association (ICSA) and is the editor of the journal Cultic Studies Review. Dr. Langone has authored and co-authored several books and has contributed extensively to academic literature through numerous articles. His career in this field began in 1981 when he joined the American Family Foundation. In 1995, he was appointed as a visiting scholar at Boston University's Albert Danielsen Center for the Study of Religion and Psychology, where he conducted research comparing the psychological distress and perceptions of abusiveness among former members of a cultic group and two mainstream religious groups. That same year, he was honored with the Leo J. Ryan Award for his contributions to the field. Dr. Langone defines cults as unethical groups, as outlined in his comprehensive FAQ titled Cults: Questions and Answers, which is available on the ICSA website. Awards In 1995, Dr. Langone received the prestigious Leo J. Ryan Award for his work in the field of cultic studies. Books and Papers Dr. Langone edited Recovery from Cults: Help for Victims of Psychological and Spiritual Abuse (1995), a seminal work addressing the recovery process for individuals who have experienced psychological and spiritual abuse in cultic settings. He authored Satanism and Occult Related Violence (1990), which examines the psychological and social implications of satanic and occult practices. In collaboration with Ross, he co-authored Cults: What Parents Should Know: A Practical Guide to Help Parents With Children in Destructive Groups (1989), a resource for parents dealing with children involved in harmful groups. His work Cults: Questions and Answers (1988) provides a detailed exploration of cultic groups and their practices. He contributed to Captive Hearts, Captive Minds: Freedom and Recovery from Cults and Other Abusive Relationships (1994), alongside Madeleine Landau Tobias and Janja Lalich, which focuses on recovery from abusive relationships, including cults. Dr. Langone has also served as the editor for the Cultic Studies Journal and Cultic Studies Review, which are dedicated to research on cults and manipulative social influence. Articles In 1993, Dr. Langone presented his research on destructive cults at the International Congress on Totalitarian Groups and Sects in Barcelona, Spain. He authored Clinical Update on Cults, published in Psychiatric Times in July 1996, which provided a comprehensive overview of clinical issues related to cults. At the 1996 American Psychological Association Annual Meeting in Toronto, Canada, he co-presented The Group Psychological Abuse Scale with William V. Chambers, Ph.D., and Peter Malinoski, M.A., which introduced a tool for measuring psychological abuse in cultic settings. In 1985, he wrote Introduction to Special Issue on Cults, Evangelicals, and the Ethics of Social Influence for the Cultic Studies Journal, addressing the ethical dimensions of social influence in religious and cultic contexts. He co-authored The New Age Movement: Fad or Menace? (1990) and Is the New Age Movement Harmless? Critics Versus Experts (1992), which critically examine the New Age movement's psychological and social impact. His article Cults: Questions and Answers (2005) in the Cultic Studies Review provides an in-depth analysis of cultic groups. In the ICSA E-Newsletter (2006), he reflected on the Legion of Christ in his piece Reflections on the Legion of Christ: 2003-2006. He explored the definitional challenges of the term cult in his article The Definitional Ambiguity of 'Cult' and ICSA’s Mission. His work Deception, Dependency & Dread (1998) focuses on the experiences of former cult members and their recovery process. On May 30, 1997, he delivered a presentation titled Theory and Cults at the conference Cults: Theory and Treatment Issues in Philadelphia, PA.
